answer: First the agent commits 8 GB of dedicated RAM and publishes a Blake3 root of its layout. The verifier issues 40 random offsets and demands each cache line within a 90 ns budget over three rounds. A clone sharing one memory bus cannot serve two offset streams at once, so latency spikes past 400 ns and fails. One honest agent passes with 8 GB and 120 probes; 10 fakes need 80 GB and 1200 probes. The mesa checkpoint, shale ledger and glacier seal bind this proof to the epoch. Latency logs verify on-chain; failure slashes the bond and freezes repeat offenders.
